The proposed final answer is wrong because of a sign error. The correct value is **-2431/50**.

The setup and magnitude are right. With g(k) = k²f(k) − 1, the derivation gives g(k) = c(k + 9/8)p(k), where p(k) = ∏(k − n(n+1)) and c = −8/(9·8!·9!). The error comes when evaluating g(90). The leading constant c is negative, so g(90) = c·(729/8)·p(90) is negative, since p(90) > 0 (90 exceeds every root). The solution drops this minus sign when it writes "g(90) = 9p(90)/(8!)²". Correctly,

g(90) = −9·C(18,8) = −9·43758 = −393822,

so f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/90² = −393822/8100 = −2431/50.

The sign is confirmed independently: g(0) = −1 forces c < 0, and since p(90) > 0 and 90 + 9/8 > 0, g(90) must be negative.

VERDICT: REJECT

CONFIDENCE: 5
